propositions: The plan-review gate lacks a standing instrument to measure whether criterion/prompt/threshold changes improve or degrade gate quality before shipping, relying only on live dogfood reviews with no systematic evaluation.

An existing corpus of ~4,300 plan_review_result_v2 sidecars with Pass-1/Pass-2/Pass-3 outputs and reconstructable plan text provides the data foundation for offline replay-based evaluation without live A/B testing.

A three-tier evaluation harness must assess Pass-1/Pass-2/Pass-3 changes in isolation (Tier-2 Opus single-criterion ~$0.17/call, Tier-1 Sonnet ~$0.5/review, Tier-0 zero-cost Pass-3 deterministic replay) while enforcing hard $200 total Bedrock budget and refusing runs exceeding remaining allocation.

Every LLM eval call must use the exact production model class (Opus for Pass-1, Sonnet for Pass-2) via Bedrock only with prompt caching enabled; the harness must record per-pass model ids and refuse to diff results across different model ids.

Changes must be judged against a noise floor derived from identical-material verdict flips (208 observed) and reproduction runs, with deltas below the noise band reported as indistinguishable rather than regressing/improving.

All tier-0 and label joins must be pure functions of a frozen offline corpus with no live-only signals; changes forbidden from substituting cheaper models to preserve budget or running passes on non-production model classes.
